lithos_version: lithos 0.5.0 @ a4d2d62; every error envelope below probed against a live Lithos (MCP serverInfo 3.2.0, 2026-10-04) except where observed_divergences says otherwise

request.notes: The whole request surface: a terminal (completed/cancelled) task back to `open`. Clears `resolved_at` and `outcome`, records the reopen as a `[Reopened]` finding (the only surviving evidence of the prior outcome — see tasks.REOPENED_FINDING_PREFIX) and emits `task.reopened`. An already-open task is `task_not_resolved`, a missing one `task_not_found`. The id is resolved from a full id OR an unambiguous prefix of at least SIX characters: a shorter one is `invalid_input` and a prefix matching more than one task is `ambiguous_id_prefix`, whose `candidates` are `{id, title}` RECORDS (capped upstream — the message says "2 or more matches" rather than a count), not id strings. Lens always sends a full id for this tool (the funnel acts on a task it has just read), so neither refusal is on a Lens request; both are vendored because the mapper must still answer them.

errors.message: task_id 'infl' is too short: pass the full task id or a prefix of at least 6 characters.
Task id prefix '506155' (task_id) is ambiguous: 2 or more matches. Retry with a longer prefix or a full id from candidates.

observed_divergences: `reblocked` is a list of task IDS, not records, and is non-empty ONLY when a *completed* blocker or gate is reopened: reopening a CANCELLED task un-strands its dependents (they were `blocker_unsatisfiable`, not ready) and re-blocks nobody — the `cancelled_reopen` variant. That is why T3 D8 counts the cancelled case from the task's own active outgoing dependency edges instead. The success payload is transcribed from the documented return (the quoted `{success, reblocked}` "plus the resolved task_id + title and the new updated_at") — it cannot be probed without reopening a real task. The `task_not_resolved` MESSAGE is likewise composed rather than probed, for the same reason; its code is what the mapper reads.
